# Global agent backlog workflow

Use the same Mac-wide Backlog.md store for all projects and Git worktrees. The
`agent-backlog` CLI changes into the canonical directory before invoking
Backlog.md. **Never** run plain `backlog` from a repository to create a new
project-local board.

- Root: `$HOME/.local/share/agent-backlog` (local-only, no Git repository).
- Board: `http://127.0.0.1:6420` (localhost only); Option-K toggles a
  dedicated Hammerspoon window.
- Start by reading `agent-backlog task list --json` and matching title,
  requirements, references and existing labels. Reuse the same task through
  follow-up questions and across sessions.
- For new actionable requests, use `agent-backlog task create "Short outcome"
  --labels "repo:<name>,area:<personal|professional>" --ac "Verifiable result"`
  when the repo and area are known; otherwise omit uncertain labels. For
  multiple distinct requests, use separate tasks. A non-repository task may
  have only an `area:` label. For known external tickets add `ticket:<id>`;
  use the canonical repository name, never a worktree slug.
- Keep concise task descriptions and acceptance criteria. Put detailed
  technical discussion in selective, brief comments, not transcript dumps.
- Add `--ref` URLs to commits, PRs or issues when available, and comments
  with exact evidence (what changed, which tests passed or failed). The board
  is a tracking view, not a substitute for Git review or CI verification.
- Record an exact session reference when exposed by the current harness,
  e.g. `Codex CLI session: <actual-id>; resume: codex resume <actual-id>`,
  or an actual ChatGPT/Claude chat permalink. Do not fabricate IDs or
  imply a chat can be reopened with one click when the tool does not support it.
- Keep tasks in To Do/In Progress when work remains or is blocked. Only
  set Done after the acceptance criteria have been verified and the user
  has accepted the result or has explicitly delegated resolution authority.
- Do not put secrets or unnecessary employer/customer data in public Git
  sources; the task store itself is deliberately local and not committed.
- No tool-specific hooks are part of this integration. Since text guidance
  cannot enforce execution in every agent runtime, report missed updates
  rather than representing them as synchronized.
